'''Alexandre Aleksandrovich Kirilloff''' ({{langx|ru|Алекса́ндр Алекса́ндрович Кири́ллов}}, born 1936) is a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n mathematician,<ref name="Marathe2010">{{cite book|last=Marathe|first=Kishore|title=Topics in Physical Mathematics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Rf7pqYEb4PQC&pg=PA420|access-date=10 August 2012|date=2010-08-18|publisher=Springer|isbn=9781848829381|pages=420–}}</ref> known for his works in the fields of [[representation theory]], [[topological group]]s and [[Lie group]]s. In particular he introduced the [[orbit method]]<ref name="Huang1999">{{cite book|last=Huang|first=Jing-Song|title=Lectures on Representation Theory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6V02ivlwC3AC&pg=PA163|access-date=10 August 2012|year=1999|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9789810237257|pages=163–}}</ref> into representation theory. He is an emeritus professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].

==Career==
Kirillov studied at [[Moscow State University]] where he was a student of [[Israel Gelfand]]. His [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] ([[kandidat]]) dissertation ''Unitary representations of nilpotent Lie groups'' was published in 1962. He was awarded the degree of [[Doctor of Science]]. At the time he was the youngest Doctor of Science in the [[Soviet Union]]. He worked at the Moscow State University until 1994 when he became the Francis J. Carey Professor of Mathematics at the University of Pennsylvania.

During his school years, Kirillov was a winner of many [[mathematics competitions]], and he is still an active organizer of Russian mathematical contests.  Kirillov is an author of many popular school-oriented books and articles.

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>

Kirillov's son, [[Alexander Kirillov, Jr.]], is also a mathematician, working on the [[Representation of a Lie group|representation theory of Lie groups]] at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]].
